title: The Dual-Population Benchmark Model
summary: Motivated by Fisher's and Hill's \cite{Fisher,Hill} ideas of ranking and pivotal quantities, we introduce a planar Poisson process (PPP) model in which the negative component \(Π_-\), acted upon by a choice operator {\rm C}, supplies a set of past benchmarks that divide the future points of the positive component \(Π_+\) into ranked categories. The benchmarks act as separators in an ordered paintbox while simultaneously acquiring the dual role of past standards established by the choice operator.
